raw_context: Urban Dictionary entry: portmanteau of 'tanga' (stupid) + 'bobo' (idiot) + 'gago' (asshole) — modern Filipino political slang describing a person with weak comprehension, used in heated political arguments on social media

Urban Dictionary entry: portmanteau of 'tanga' (stupid) + 'Tagalog' — used on international imageboards to annoy anonymous Filipinos; 2025 variation 'Tangalog Syndrome' describes native Luzon folk who code-switch to English mid-sentence to sound sophisticated

Urban Dictionary 2025 variant: 'a chronic linguistic disorder found mostly among native Luzon folks who suddenly feel the need to speak in English halfway through a sentence just to sound smart or relate-worthy'

Urban Dictionary entry: 'Petiks na naman si Juaning, pa-relax-relax lang, hindi inaasikaso trabaho n'ya.' — slang for procrastinator or someone who habitually unwinds; also used as verb meaning to take a break; Talkpal Gen Z usage notes newer meaning of 'faking/pretending'

Urban Dictionary entry 'ala me pakels': mashup of wala (none) + me (English) + pakialam (care/concern) = 'I don't care'; 'Hey I heard they were talking shit about you.' 'No way? Oh well, ala me pakels.'
Urban Dictionary full phrase: 'I don't care' — 'ala' from 'wala' (nothing), 'me' English, 'pakels' from 'pakialam' (concern); used in dismissive response to drama or gossip

PEP.ph Gen Z lingo guide: 'Lavarn is a popularized Filipino Gen Z word derived from the Tagalog word Laban (fight/keep going)'; 'Kahit di ka na mag-champion sis, i-lavarn mo pa din.' — Bekimon/swardspeak evolution of laban

PEP.ph Gen Z lingo: 'Pa-mine means to claim ownership of something shown on screen; derived from the live-selling community'; 'Ang sarap tignan ng mango float, pa-mine naman niyan, sis.' — from livestream shopping culture

PEP.ph: 'The slang phrase amaccana accla is used to denote problematic or inappropriate conduct. Amaccana is from Tama ka na (You stop it), and accla is derived from bakla.' — gay lingo / swardspeak phrase

PEP.ph Gen Z lingo: 'Pala-desisyon is used to call out a person's tendency to comment in a decisive or judgmental manner'; 'Wag kang pala-desisyon, beh!' — used to call someone out for being overly opinionated

Manila Bulletin Jan 2026: 'Inspired by rapper Skrilla's song Doot Doot (6 7). 6-7 can mean anything — so-so, maybe, I don't know, or sometimes nothing at all. Its versatility combined with a hand gesture (palms up, moving up and down) made it irresistible to younger users. Dictionary.com named it Word of 2025.'

Manila Bulletin Jan 2026: 'Short for uncool or uncle, this word has been in Gen Alpha's dictionary since 2023. It is now used to describe anyone who seems out of touch — anyone or anything that is out of style, outdated, or not cool.'

Manila Bulletin Jan 2026: 'Derived from the acronym AMOG (Alpha Male Of Group) and popularized through gaming, social media, and meme culture in 2025, to mog someone means to outperform or outshine them — in style, skills, or social presence.' 'She mogged everyone in the school talent show.'

Urban Dictionary entry: 'A famous Filipino word often used to express strong feeling. It originally means poop/dump but started being used as a general expression, mostly among Gen Z kids. It can be used in any part of a sentence — whether you're angry, happy, or surprised.' — evolved exclamation usage documented 2023-2026

Multiple sources: 'Sana all literally translates to I wish all — a common response to someone else having or experiencing something you want. It can also be used in aspirational sense, e.g. seeing a sweet couple: sanaol!' — Foodega 2024: 'May boyfriend na siya, sana all!'

FastForward MR Filipino Gen Z Dictionary: 'Benchwarmer refers to a person kept as a backup romantic option — someone held in reserve in case the primary relationship or talking stage doesn't work out.' — modern Filipino dating slang prominent in 2020s social media discourse
